## Error Handling

### Error Scenario 1: migration script — source bucket does not exist

**Condition**: a source bucket listed in `MIGRATION_MAPPING` is not accessible (404 / NoSuchBucket or AccessDenied).
**Response**: if `entry.optional=True`, log a warning and mark the entry as skipped. If `entry.optional=False`, log an error, record `verified=False` in the report, and exit non-zero at the end.
**Recovery**: operator inspects the report, reruns with `--verify-only` after resolving the access issue.

### Error Scenario 2: migration script — object count mismatch after sync

**Condition**: post-sync `count_objects(source) != count_objects(dest)`.
**Response**: record `verified=False` in the report for that entry; do not delete any source data; continue to the next entry. Exit code 1 at the end.
**Recovery**: operator inspects the diff (typically a race with new writes — re-run the sync targeting the specific entry, then `--verify-only`).

### Error Scenario 3: CDK deploy — stack already exists with an older config

**Condition**: deploying `CCETStorage-{Env}` when a bucket named `ccet-{env}` already exists but is not owned by this stack.
**Response**: CloudFormation returns `BucketAlreadyExists` or `BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou`; the CDK `cdk deploy` fails.
**Recovery**: this cannot happen under normal operation because bucket names are globally unique. If it does (bucket squatting), the operator must pick a different name — flag as a manual remediation step in the runbook.

### Error Scenario 4: Firehose reconfiguration — in-flight records buffered at cutover

**Condition**: Firehose has un-flushed records when the CloudFormation update changes the destination prefix.
**Response**: Per the [AWS Firehose UpdateDestination API documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateDestination.html): *"The target Firehose stream remains active while the configurations are updated, so data writes to the Firehose stream can continue during this process. The updated configurations are usually effective within a few minutes."* The documentation does NOT explicitly specify which destination receives records that were buffered at the moment of the update — they may land on the new destination (not the old one) once the update takes effect. This means up to 60 seconds or 64 MB of records (the raw-archive Firehose buffer limits, per `cdk/data_pipeline/stack.py` `buffering_hints`) could potentially land on the new bucket while an operator still considers the old one "active". Correction to an earlier draft of this design: Do not claim the buffer "drains to the OLD destination" — that claim is not in the AWS documentation.
**Recovery**: Run the migration script with `--verify-only` **twice** post-cutover: once immediately after the Firehose update is `UpdateStatus=ACTIVE` (to catch any records that did land on the new bucket), and again after the Firehose buffer window has fully elapsed (≥65 seconds wait) to catch any straggler records on either bucket. If any objects appear on the old bucket after the second pass, re-run `aws s3 sync` targeting the specific prefixes and re-verify.

### Error Scenario 5: RL training CANDIDATE records reference old bucket

**Condition**: a CANDIDATE record created before migration has `s3_bucket=ccet-ml-models-{env}` and `s3_prefix=models/dqn/{version}/`. Post-migration, that bucket no longer exists.
**Response**: `promotion_handler` Lambda fails with "bucket not found" when verifying artifacts.
**Recovery**: either (a) retrain to create a fresh CANDIDATE record with the new bucket, or (b) run a one-shot script to UPDATE existing CANDIDATE records' `s3_bucket` field. Option (b) is preferable and is listed as an explicit task below.

### Error Scenario 6: Noncurrent object versions discarded on source bucket deletion (per Prompt 5 A6)

**Condition**: `ccet-ml-datasets-{env}` and `ccet-ml-models-{env}` have `Versioning=Enabled` and therefore accumulated noncurrent object versions + delete markers over their lifetime. `aws s3 sync` migrates only current versions. When Task 26 iterates `list-object-versions` to empty each source bucket before `rb`, every noncurrent version and delete marker is permanently destroyed.
**Response**: this is the accepted user decision (Prompt 5 userInput — option a). The new bucket is `versioned=False`, so there is no destination to receive noncurrent versions. Historical noncurrent versions are treated as ephemeral snapshots — consistent with the user's non-goal of preserving versioning on the new bucket.
**Recovery**: none. Users needing pre-migration history must consult the `archive/legacy-training-data-backup/` prefix (copied as current versions during migration) or the baseline snapshot taken at Task 29.1 (if still available).

## Post-Review Clarifications (Prompt 4)

This section documents design-level decisions triggered by the Prompt 4 critical review. These are **not separate architectural components** — they are clarifications to existing sections that would otherwise be ambiguous.

### A1 — `cdk/shared/common_constructs.py::CCETFirehoseDeliveryStream` audit

**Finding**: The reusable `CCETFirehoseDeliveryStream` construct (`cdk/shared/common_constructs.py`) accepts the destination bucket as a constructor parameter (`s3_destination_bucket: Union[s3.Bucket, s3.IBucket]`) and grants IAM via `s3_destination_bucket.grant_read_write(firehose_role)`. **No hardcoded bucket names or ARNs exist in this construct.** The retargeting done at each call site (Tasks 7 and 8) is therefore complete — no additional task is required for `common_constructs.py` itself. This is recorded as an explicit verification step in Task 7.

### A4/A5 — SageMaker endpoint DataCaptureConfig

**Finding**: `src/ml/training/model_registry.py` lines 585-588 explicitly state: *"SageMaker Serverless Inference does not support DataCaptureConfig. Data capture is omitted for serverless endpoints. If real-time instance-based endpoints are used in the future, re-enable DataCaptureConfig here."* The current SageMaker endpoints (`ccet-xgboost-{env}`, `ccet-dqn-endpoint-{env}`) are Serverless Inference endpoints and therefore do **not** write to the old `ccet-ml-models-{env}/data-capture/` prefix. The migration mapping entry for `data-capture/` → `inference-logs/` will copy zero objects in today's deployment; no KMS key is in play; no UpdateEndpoint call is required. The `inference-logs/` prefix on the new bucket is reserved for future use if real-time instance-based endpoints are introduced (a Phase 2 concern). This resolves both A4 and A5. The user's original concerns (endpoint re-deployment, KMS mismatch) are **not applicable to the current codebase**.

### A8 — Legacy training-data-backup retention

**Finding**: The `training-data-backup/` prefix on `ccet-ml-datasets-dev` contains historical Firehose data copied during an out-of-band bucket recreation on 2026-04-24 (per `docs/s3-storage-structure.md`). The user flagged this as a "backup in case we mess up this activity" (Prompt 1 Section A.3, answer to A7). Migrating this data under `temp/legacy-training-data-backup/` (14-day expiration) would contradict its purpose. **Decision**: the migration target is changed to `archive/legacy-training-data-backup/`, under a new top-level `archive/` prefix with **no expiration**. The new `CCETStorageStack` has exactly one lifecycle rule (`TempExpiration` on `temp/`) — the `archive/` prefix is explicitly excluded from any lifecycle. Truly-dead `training-data/` data continues to land in `temp/legacy-training-data/` (14-day expiration is appropriate).

### C1 — SSM bootstrap circularity

**Finding**: If any Lambda handler resolves `/ccet/{env}/storage/bucket-name` at module import time (cold-start, before the first invocation), a bootstrap deploy on an empty account could fail because the SSM parameter doesn't exist yet. **Decision**: every Lambda handler that reads the storage bucket name MUST resolve it **lazily** (on first invocation, not at module import). A property-test case is added to Task 22 to assert that module import alone (no invocation) does not trigger an SSM call. This is documented in Testing Strategy § "Integration Testing Approach".

### C2 — Migration verification method (Req 7.2)

**Finding**: Requirement 7.2's "byte-for-byte" wording is stricter than `aws s3 sync` provides. `aws s3 sync --exact-timestamps` compares size + last-modified — not content hashes. ETag is only an MD5 for single-part uploads; for multipart uploads it is a hash-of-hashes and cannot be used for cross-bucket content equality. **Decision**: Requirement 7.2 is **weakened** to "object count parity + per-object size parity", which is exactly what the migration script can and will verify (via `list_objects_v2` pagination comparing `KeyCount` and `Size` per key). The migration script is updated to record per-object size in the JSON report, and the report verification asserts size parity per key, not just count parity.

### C5 — `--skip-migration-check` flag

**Finding**: Req 13.3 marked the `--skip-migration-check` flag as "(Optional)". **Decision**: the flag is **committed to implementation** (not aspirational). Task 13-new (§ below in tasks.md) implements the pre-flight check + flag.

### D5 — SageMaker default bucket literal exception

**Finding**: `cdk/ml_pipeline/constructs.py` line 260 uses `f"sagemaker-{region}-{account_id}"` as an intentional reference to the AWS-managed SageMaker default bucket (imported by `s3.Bucket.from_bucket_name`). This is explicitly out-of-scope for the consolidation (the user specified keeping shared AWS-managed buckets unchanged in the non-goals). **Decision**: the CI guardrail added in Task 23 adds `sagemaker-{region}-{account}` to a soft-warn list (not a block), with an approved-exception allowlist entry for `cdk/ml_pipeline/constructs.py::_create_sagemaker_execution_role`. Other occurrences (e.g., new code) would be flagged.

---

## Post-Review Clarifications (Prompt 5)

This section documents design-level decisions triggered by the Prompt 5 second critical review (A1–A7, B1–B4, C1–C7, D1–D5). All A/B items required specific design changes or explicit user decisions; C/D items are mostly clarifications.

### A1 — Canonical sentinel JSON shape (Req 18.4 adopted)

**Finding**: Req 7.6, Req 13.2, Req 13.4, and Task 13a previously described three incompatible formats for `/ccet/{env}/storage/migration-complete`: plain `"true"`, JSON with `completed_at`, and a "legacy-value fallback". **Decision (per Prompt 5 A1)**: Req 18.4's JSON shape is adopted as the single canonical format:

```json
{"completed_at": "<ISO-8601 UTC>", "script_version": "<git-sha-or-tag>", "mapping_entries_verified": <int>}
```

No legacy `"true"` fallback is accepted. Req 7.6 and Req 13.2/13.4 are updated in `requirements.md` to reference Req 18.4. Task 13a (pre-flight check) parses the value as JSON and asserts `completed_at` is present; any non-JSON value or missing `completed_at` fails the pre-flight. Task 19 (migration script) writes the canonical shape via `ssm.put_parameter(Overwrite=True)` per the ALGORITHM above. There is no deployed consumer of the legacy string form — this is a new parameter introduced in this spec.

### A2 — `archive/` prefix added to R3.1 enumeration

**Finding**: Req 3.1 previously enumerated 9 prefixes but omitted `archive/`, which the migration script populates (Req 7) and which Task 22 smoke tests write under. **Decision**: `archive/` is added to the Req 3.1 enumeration. The authoritative prefix list is now 9 prefixes: `raw/`, `raw-errors/`, `processed/v1-horizon2min-window30min/`, `processed/v2-horizon30min-window60min/`, `models/`, `code/`, `reports/`, `inference-logs/`, `archive/`, `temp/`. Correctness Property 10 (above) is corrected from "10 top-level prefixes" to "9 top-level prefixes" (D2 fix).

### A3 — `cdk/shared/config.py` deprecated-aliases contradiction resolved

**Finding**: The "Low-Level Design — Code Change Surface" table's `cdk/shared/config.py` row previously said "Keep the two old fields as deprecated aliases for one release cycle" while Task 4 said "Delete the old fields immediately". **Decision**: design table is updated to match Task 4 (delete immediately, no aliases). See the updated row above.

### A4 — Per-env Task 29 gating (rolled out in tasks.md)

**Finding**: Task 27 (stage/prod rollout) previously ran Task 24 directly with no Task 29 gate before Task 25/26 on stage/prod. **Decision**: Task 27 is rewritten as 27.1–27.6 interleaving Task 24 → Task 29 → Task 25/26 per environment. See `tasks.md` Task 27 — stage and prod deletions are now explicitly gated on per-environment E2E PASS.

### A5 — Explicit env/ssm_base_path resolution source per Lambda / script

**Finding**: Tasks 12–16 previously said "Read bucket name from SSM `/ccet/{env}/storage/bucket-name`" without specifying how each handler resolves `env`. Grep evidence confirms the current handlers do NOT use an `ssm_base_path` pattern (no matches in `src/lambdas/rl_training_pipeline/`). **Decision**: each task specifies the env-resolution source explicitly:

| Module | Env resolution source |
|---|---|
| `src/lambdas/rl_training_pipeline/data_export_handler.py` (Task 12) | Extract from the state-machine event payload. Step Functions is updated (Task 11) to pass `ssm_base_path="/ccet/{env}/storage/"` in the event, and the handler calls `get_ssm_param_path(base_path=event["ssm_base_path"], param_name="bucket-name")`. |
| `src/lambdas/rl_training_pipeline/registration_handler.py` (Task 13) | Same pattern — extract `ssm_base_path` from the state-machine event. |
| `src/ml/training/sagemaker_pipeline.py` + `sagemaker_training.py` + `model_registry.py` (Task 14) | These are CDK-construction-time modules. They read from `config.storage_bucket_name` (`CCETConfiguration`) passed as a constructor arg — no runtime SSM lookup needed. |
| `src/ml/training/data_loader.py` (Task 15) | Runs inside SageMaker training containers. SageMaker is explicitly out-of-scope for the `no-environment-vars.md` rule per workspace policy precedent in `CCETTrainingEnvironment`. Pass the bucket name via SageMaker training-job hyperparameters (`hyperparameters={"storage_bucket_name": config.storage_bucket_name}`). The loader reads `bucket_name` from its already-existing `__init__(bucket_name: str, ...)` parameter — no change to its signature. |
| `src/benchmarking/report_generator.py` (Task 16) | Called by the Metrics Lambda. The Metrics Lambda extracts `ssm_base_path` from its invocation event (CloudWatch Events-scheduled — CDK is updated to inject `ssm_base_path` into the input transformer) and passes the resolved bucket name to `write_report_to_s3(bucket_name=…)`. |
| Any CDK-construction-time code (Tasks 5–11) | Reads `config.storage_bucket_name` from `CCETConfiguration` directly — no runtime SSM lookup. |

This removes the ambiguity flagged in Prompt 5 A5.

### A6 — Noncurrent object versions discarded (user decision, option a)

**Finding**: Both source buckets have `Versioning=Enabled` (drifts D1/D2). `aws s3 sync` migrates current versions only. **User decision (via userInput in Prompt 5)**: option (a) — accept loss of noncurrent versions and delete markers; they are treated as ephemeral snapshots consistent with `versioned=False` on the new bucket. **Decision**: design is updated to reflect this explicitly in:
- The ALGORITHM pseudocode above (note at the top of the block).
- The migration mapping table (already marks `training-data-backup/` → `archive/` to preserve user-designated recovery data; other prefixes inherit the current-versions-only semantics).
- New Error Scenario 6 (above).
- `docs/storage.md` (Task 21 extended to document the discard decision and its rationale).

### A7 — AWS SSE-S3 default encryption (user concern validated, Req 1.2 rewritten)

**Finding (verified via AWS doc)**: [AWS S3 UsingEncryption docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingEncryption.html) state: *"Amazon S3 now applies server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) as the base level of encryption for every bucket in Amazon S3. Starting January 5, 2023, all new object uploads to Amazon S3 are automatically encrypted at no additional cost and with no impact on performance."* **Decision**: Req 1.2 is weakened per the user's proposed text:

> WHEN `aws s3api get-bucket-encryption` is invoked, THEN the response MUST NOT contain any `KmsKeyId` or `KmsMasterKeyID`. The default AWS-managed SSE-S3 (AES256) is acceptable and expected per AWS's post-2023 default-encryption policy.

Correctness Property 5 (above) is updated to match. The smoke test `smoke_test_no_encryption` (Task 22) is updated to match: assert no `KmsKeyId`/`KmsMasterKeyID`, accept an `SSEAlgorithm=AES256` response as the AWS default.

### B1 — Archive retention decision (user selected option a — indefinite)

**Finding**: user's original Prompt 1 phrasing "only for backup in case we mess up this activity" could defensibly map to either indefinite retention or a time-bounded `archive/` + expiration. **User decision (via userInput in Prompt 5)**: option (a) — keep indefinite retention for `archive/legacy-training-data-backup/`; user retains manual control to delete after Task 29 PASS. **Decision**: `docs/storage.md` (Task 21) and the Prefix Taxonomy User Intent Note above both explicitly state this as a conservative interpretation of "backup" with manual user control. No CDK lifecycle rule is ever added for `archive/`.

### B2 — CI user IAM audit added (grep evidence)

**Finding (verified via `grepSearch` against `cdk/ci_iam/stack.py`)**: line 50 contains `"s3:*"` in `CDK_DEPLOY_ACTIONS`, applied as an `Allow` on `Resource=*` (all buckets). There are NO old-bucket-name literals, but the wildcard grant means the CI user can write to any bucket — including the old `ccet-ml-datasets-{env}` etc. during the window before Task 26 empties them. This would make the negative tests in Task 29.10 a false positive (the CI user could in fact write to an old bucket).

**Decision**: a new Task 9a is added to `tasks.md` that audits `cdk/ci_iam/stack.py`, `cdk/ci_iam/prod_ci_user_stack.py`, `cdk/ci_iam/stage_ci_user_stack.py` for S3 IAM statements and retargets the CI user's S3 grants to `ccet-{env}` with prefix-scoped access via `PrefixScopedGrant`. The wildcard `s3:*` on `*` is tightened to (at most) `s3:*` on `arn:aws:s3:::ccet-{env}` + `arn:aws:s3:::ccet-{env}/*` + the CDK staging bucket `arn:aws:s3:::cdk-hnb659fds-assets-*` (required for CDK deploy). Any CI-user S3 test-writes are restricted to CCET-controlled prefixes only.

### B3 — Req 15.2 moved from requirements.md to design.md (aspirational clause)

**Finding**: Req 15.2 described a future-state invariant ("WHEN future code re-enables DataCaptureConfig for real-time endpoints, THEN `DestinationS3Uri` MUST resolve to `s3://ccet-{env}/inference-logs/{endpoint_name}/`") that cannot be tested today — current codebase uses SageMaker Serverless Inference which does not support DataCaptureConfig (verified at `src/ml/training/model_registry.py:585-588`). **Decision**: Req 15.2 is removed from `requirements.md`. Its content is moved here as a forward-compatibility design note:

> **Forward-compat note (formerly Req 15.2)**: If future code re-enables `DataCaptureConfig` for real-time instance-based SageMaker endpoints, the `DestinationS3Uri` MUST resolve to `s3://ccet-{env}/inference-logs/{endpoint_name}/` — read from SSM `/ccet/{env}/storage/bucket-name`. The code comment at `src/ml/training/model_registry.py:585-588` is updated in Task 14 to document this intended destination. A CI guardrail in Task 23 flags any new `KmsKeyId` occurrences in `src/ml/training/` for reviewer attention (bucket is unencrypted aside from AWS-default SSE-S3, so a KMS-based DataCaptureConfig would fail).

This is a design note only — not a verifiable Phase 1 acceptance criterion.

### B4 — Req 5.7 rewritten as conditional

**Finding**: Req 5.7 asserted "WHEN a SageMaker endpoint is invoked post-cutover, THEN data-capture records are written to `s3://ccet-{env}/inference-logs/*`" — but Req 15.1 documents that no current endpoint writes data capture (Serverless Inference limitation). Req 5.7 is vacuously true today. **Decision**: Req 5.7 is rewritten as a conditional in `requirements.md`:

> IF any SageMaker endpoint writes data capture records post-cutover, THEN records MUST land under `inference-logs/*`.

Verifiability: Task 29.8 confirms data-capture is OFF (no new objects at `inference-logs/`); if/when it is enabled, the same smoke test serves as the forward-gate.

### C1 — Task 29 numbering (EXECUTION ORDER header added)

**Decision**: a prominent EXECUTION ORDER callout is added to the top of `tasks.md` showing: `1 → 2 → ... → 24 → 29 → 25 → 26 → 27 → 28`. Tasks are not renumbered (to preserve prior-commit references) — the callout makes the order explicit. See `tasks.md` top-of-file.

### C2 — `--force-ignore-training-jobs` semantics documented

**Decision**: Task 19 amended — when `--force-ignore-training-jobs` is used, the script logs a WARNING and records `force_ignore_training_jobs=true` in the JSON report (see ALGORITHM above). The sentinel SSM parameter is still written on success (so deploy pre-flight continues to pass); the operator's decision to force-proceed is captured in the audit trail.

### C3 — Task 29.11 HTTP-probe wording

**Decision**: Task 29.11 clarified — only the HTTPS probe creates an object, so cleanup is required only for the HTTPS path. The HTTP-PUT assertion accepts either `AccessDenied` OR a TCP-level connection error (if AWS rejects the non-TLS connection entirely before evaluating the policy) as a valid denial signal. See `tasks.md` Task 29.11.

### C4 — `_step_check_health` presence verified

**Finding (verified via `grepSearch` against `cdk/deploy.py`)**: `_step_check_health` EXISTS at line 336. The user's concern that "Kiro will guess" the function name is preempted by the verified evidence. **Decision**: Task 13a is reframed per the user's instruction to avoid coupling the pre-flight to a specific internal step function — the task now says "add a new pre-flight check step in the deploy sequence, executed before any stack deploy (except `CCETStorage-{Env}` itself)". The implementer may choose either to extend `_step_check_health` or to add a new `_step_check_migration_sentinel` — both are acceptable as long as the behavior (read SSM, parse JSON, assert `completed_at`, raise `CCETDeploymentException` on failure) is correct.

Plus any Lambda handler module created or modified by Tasks 14 (SageMaker-side — out of test scope) / 16 (benchmarking — the `report_generator` module above). See `tasks.md` Task 22.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Testing Approach

- **CDK unit tests** (`test/cdk/storage/test_storage_stack.py`): synthesize the stack in isolation, assert (a) bucket properties via `Template.from_stack(...).has_resource_properties("AWS::S3::Bucket", ...)`, (b) lifecycle rule presence, (c) tag set, (d) SSL policy, (e) auto-delete-on-dev semantics, (f) SSM parameter creation. Reference pattern: existing `test/cdk/benchmarking_pipeline/test_constructs.py`.
- **Migration script unit tests** (`test/scripts/test_migrate_s3_storage.py`): mock `subprocess.run` and `s3.list_objects_v2`. Assert the mapping table is complete, verification logic is correct, dry-run mode never shells out to `aws s3 sync`.
- **IAM construct unit tests** (`test/cdk/storage/test_prefix_scoped_grant.py`): synth a stack with a `PrefixScopedGrant`, assert the resulting IAM policy document matches the shape documented above (no `s3:*`, no `{bucket}/*` without prefix).

### Property-Based Testing Approach

**Property Test Library**: `hypothesis` (per existing project conventions).

Target properties:
1. **Prefix-taxonomy exclusivity** — for any generated `PrefixGrant.prefix`, the resulting IAM policy statement's `Resource` ends with `{prefix}*` and nothing else.
2. **No-wildcard invariant** — for any `PrefixScopedGrant` with any non-empty grant list, no generated `PolicyStatement` has `Action="s3:*"` or `Resource=f"{bucket_arn}/*"`.
3. **Migration idempotency** — running the migration script twice with `--verify-only` produces the same report (modulo timestamps).
4. **SSM path round-trip** — `_extract_env_from_ssm_base_path(get_storage_ssm_path(env))` returns `env` for all valid env strings.

### Integration Testing Approach

- Extend `test/integration/smoke/test_rl_pipeline.py` to verify the new training-code S3 key.
- Add `test/integration/smoke/test_storage.py` with:
  - `smoke_test_consolidated_bucket_exists` — `s3api head-bucket ccet-{env}` returns 200.
  - `smoke_test_lifecycle_rule` — `s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration` returns exactly one rule with `Prefix=temp/` and `ExpirationInDays=14`.
  - `smoke_test_ssl_enforcement` — `s3api get-bucket-policy` returns a deny statement on `aws:SecureTransport=false`. Additionally, a Python `boto3` PUT via HTTPS is asserted to succeed (boto3 defaults to HTTPS — confirms the SDK and the policy agree); an HTTP-forced PUT is asserted to fail with `AccessDenied` (defense in depth against regressions). (Per A6 clarification.)
  - `smoke_test_no_encryption` — `s3api get-bucket-encryption` returns `ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError` (or the equivalent CDK `UNENCRYPTED` shape) and `s3api get-bucket-versioning` returns empty (not `Enabled`).
  - `smoke_test_tags` — `s3api get-bucket-tagging` returns exactly `Project=CCET, Environment={env}, ManagedBy=CDK, Owner=ccet-team`.
  - `smoke_test_temp_put_delete` — put a small object under `temp/smoke/` and delete it (validates write + delete + SSL-only).
  - `smoke_test_archive_no_lifecycle` — put a small object under `archive/smoke/`, list bucket lifecycle, assert the `archive/` prefix matches **no** lifecycle rule (C2 / A8).
  - `smoke_test_lambda_cold_start_no_ssm_at_import` — import each modified Lambda handler module in isolation (without invoking `handler()`), assert no `ssm:GetParameter` call was made (mock `boto3.client('ssm')` and count calls). This catches regressions to lazy-SSM resolution per C1.
- All smoke tests follow the existing pattern in `test/integration/smoke/` (180s budget, `SimulatePrincipalPolicy` for IAM checks where needed).

## Security Considerations

- **SSL-only**: `enforce_ssl=True` on the consolidated bucket generates a bucket policy denying all non-TLS requests, matching the AWS documented pattern at [Enforcing encryption in transit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingEncryptionInTransit.html#enforcing-encryption-in-transit).
- **Block public access**: `BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL` set; verified by smoke test.
- **Least-privilege IAM**: every principal's policy lists explicit prefixes; no `s3:*` or bucket-wide resource grants. Audited by the `no-wildcard IAM invariant` property test (section above) and by CDK Nag rule `AwsSolutions-IAM5` (where applicable).
- **No encryption**: per explicit user directive. The spec acknowledges this means data at rest is not encrypted — suitable for dev; a follow-up Phase 2 can re-visit for stage/prod if the threat model changes.
- **No versioning**: per explicit user directive. Combined with the non-goal of a re-drive mechanism in Phase 1, the durable source of truth for raw data is the new `raw/` prefix (Firehose-appended only) and DynamoDB (which has streams + TTL).
- **Tag-based access control**: `Project=CCET` tag enables future organization-wide SCPs that restrict action to tagged resources. Not relied on in Phase 1 but enabled.
- **2021 legacy bucket deletion**: `ccet` and `ccet-test` contain 2021-era artifacts with delete markers but still hold historical versions. Deletion requires `s3api delete-object` with `VersionId` for each historical version then `s3 rb --force`. Document in the runbook; authorize now per user directive.

---

## Performance Considerations

- **Migration data volume**: the three existing buckets together hold GZIP archives back to 2025-08 under `processed/v*/` and `training-data-backup/`. `aws s3 sync` with default concurrency (10 parallel uploads) on a single host will move ~several GB in minutes for dev. Stage/prod TBD based on actual object counts.
- **Firehose cutover latency**: CloudFormation `UpdateDestination` on a Firehose delivery stream is a sub-minute operation per AWS docs ([UpdateDestination](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateDestination.html)). In-flight behavior for buffered records is not explicitly documented by AWS; Error Scenario 4 covers the verification approach (run `--verify-only` twice with a buffer-flush wait in between). No additional latency on the hot data path (DynamoDB remains authoritative).
- **SSM read contention**: adding `/ccet/{env}/storage/bucket-name` introduces one SSM read per stack at synth time and one per Lambda cold start (in handlers that now read the bucket name from SSM). SSM throughput quota is 1000 TPS per account per region — negligible impact.
- **Lifecycle rule evaluation**: S3 evaluates lifecycle rules once per day; the single `temp/` prefix rule has no meaningful performance cost.

## Risks and Mitigations

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Firehose cutover drops in-flight records | Low | Medium | Old bucket retained during migration; any stragglers copied by a second `--verify-only` pass; documented in the runbook. |
| 2 | CANDIDATE records in model registry reference the deleted bucket | Medium | High | Add explicit task to update all CANDIDATE records' `s3_bucket` field before deleting the old bucket. Block old-bucket deletion on this step. |
| 3 | Downstream code still has a hardcoded `ccet-ml-models-{env}` after the refactor | Medium | Medium | Grep-based CI check (new lint rule): no occurrences of `ccet-ml-datasets-` or `ccet-ml-models-` or `ccet-benchmark-reports-` as string literals outside this spec's doc files. |
| 4 | CDK snapshot tests break widely after the refactor | High | Low | Expected — regenerate snapshots atomically in the same PR. Task list reflects this. |
| 5 | Operator forgets to run `migrate_s3_storage.py` between stacks 1 and 2 | Low | High | `cdk/deploy.py` gains an explicit pre-flight check: if `/ccet/{env}/storage/migration-complete` sentinel SSM parameter is missing, is not valid JSON, or is missing a `completed_at` field, fail downstream deploys with a clear error instructing the operator to run migration (per Prompt 5 A1 canonical JSON shape — Req 18.4). `--skip-migration-check` flag allows re-deploys after migration has been performed. (A3, C5.) |
| 6 | Legacy bucket deletion triggers a Python traceback in some forgotten cron job | Low | Medium | Grep all `scripts/` and `src/` for `ccet-ml-datasets|ccet-ml-models|ccet-benchmark-reports` after refactor — this is an acceptance criterion. |
| 7 | CloudFormation orphans the three old project buckets when their definitions are removed from CDK code | High | Medium | Explicit AWS CLI–based deletion procedure in Task 26 (empty versioned `ccet-ml-datasets-{env}` via `list-object-versions` + `delete-objects`, then `rb`). CloudFormation cannot delete retained-then-removed resources per [AWS DeletionPolicy docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html). (C4.) |
| 8 | In-flight SageMaker training/HPO jobs reference old bucket URIs at cutover | Low | Medium | Task 24 adds a pre-flight `aws sagemaker list-training-jobs --status-equals InProgress` check; migration is blocked until no InProgress jobs exist. (B3.) |
| 9 | CANDIDATE model-registry records have `s3_prefix=training-data/...` which maps to `temp/rl-training-exports/...` (not just a bucket rename) | Medium | Medium | Task 20 updated to use the full migration mapping for prefix remapping, not just bucket-name rewriting. (C3.) |

- [ ] 13a. Implement deploy-orchestrator migration pre-flight check (NEW per Prompt 4 A3, C5; revised per Prompt 5 A1 + C4)
  - **Task framing (per Prompt 5 C4)**: add a new pre-flight check step in the `cdk/deploy.py` deploy sequence, executed **before any stack deploy EXCEPT `CCETStorage-{Env}` itself** (the storage stack must be deployable before migration runs; otherwise there is no destination bucket). The implementer MAY either (a) extend the existing `_step_check_health` or (b) add a new private step method such as `_step_check_migration_sentinel`. Both are acceptable — the task does NOT prescribe a specific function name. Evidence (verified via `grepSearch`): `_step_check_health` exists at `cdk/deploy.py` line 336, but the choice of extension point is left to the implementer.
  - **Sentinel format — single canonical shape (per Prompt 5 A1)**: the pre-flight reads SSM parameter `/ccet/{env}/storage/migration-complete`. The value MUST parse as JSON matching the canonical shape defined in Req 18.4:
    ```json
    {"completed_at": "<ISO-8601>", "script_version": "<git-sha-or-tag>", "mapping_entries_verified": <int>}
    ```
    The pre-flight asserts the parsed JSON has a `completed_at` field of non-empty string type. Any non-JSON value, missing parameter, or missing `completed_at` fails the check with a `CCETDeploymentException` instructing the operator to run `python scripts/migrate_s3_storage.py --environment {env}`. **No legacy plain-string `"true"` value is accepted** — this parameter is introduced fresh in this spec and has no legacy consumers.
  - Add `--skip-migration-check` CLI flag (dest `ARG_SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECK`) that bypasses the pre-flight. Per Req 13.3 / Req 18.3: this flag MUST be implemented (not optional).
  - When `CCETStorage-{Env}` is the only stack being deployed (e.g., `--stacks CCETStorage-Dev`), the pre-flight MUST NOT trigger.
  - Write unit tests for all four paths:
    - (a) sentinel present and parseable with `completed_at` present → pre-flight passes;
    - (b) sentinel missing + no flag → `CCETDeploymentException` raised;
    - (c) sentinel present but NOT valid JSON (or JSON without `completed_at`) → `CCETDeploymentException` raised with a message distinguishing the parse failure from the missing-parameter case;
    - (d) sentinel missing + `--skip-migration-check` → pre-flight skipped.
  - *Design: "Risks and Mitigations" § Risk 5 mitigation, "Post-Review Clarifications (Prompt 4)" § A3, C5, "Post-Review Clarifications (Prompt 5)" § A1 + C4*
  - *Requirements: R13, R18*

Target the same `s3://ccet-{env}/temp/probe.txt`. **Assert the PUT is denied** — the assertion accepts EITHER `AccessDenied` (bucket policy with `aws:SecureTransport=false` deny) OR a TCP-level connection error / `EndpointConnectionError` (if AWS rejects the non-TLS connection entirely before policy evaluation — per Prompt 5 C3: boto3 with `use_ssl=False` connects to `http://s3.{region}.amazonaws.com`; if the endpoint refuses the TCP connection, a connection error is raised instead of a `ClientError`, and both outcomes prove the HTTP path is closed). - [ ] 26. Retire old project buckets (AWS CLI procedure per C4 rewrite)
  > **GATE**: Only execute after Task 29 completes with PASS AND Task 25 is complete (Req 16).
  >
  > **Per Prompt 4 item C4**: Once Task 7/8/9 remove the bucket definitions from the CDK source, the three live buckets become "orphaned" — they persist physically but CloudFormation no longer manages them (per [AWS DeletionPolicy docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html): *"If a resource is deleted, the `DeletionPolicy` retains the physical resource but ensures that it's deleted from CloudFormation's scope."*). A subsequent CDK PR that toggles `RemovalPolicy.DESTROY` + `auto_delete_objects=True` **cannot** delete them because they are no longer in any stack template. Deletion must therefore be done via AWS CLI.

  - [ ] 26.1 Empty and delete `ccet-ml-datasets-{env}` (versioning-enabled per drift D1 — requires explicit version deletion):
    ```bash
    # Profile is resolved from src.aws_config.AWSConfig.get_account(env).profile
    # per Prompt 5 D4 — NOT hardcoded bestehorn-learning (which is dev-only).
    # This makes the script reusable on stage and prod.
    ENV=dev
    # Resolve profile + region via Python helper (see scripts/delete_versioned_bucket.py below)
    PROFILE=$(python -c "from src.aws_config import aws_config; print(aws_config.get_account('${ENV}').profile)")
    REGION=$(python -c "from src.aws_config import aws_config; print(aws_config.get_account('${ENV}').region)")
    BUCKET=ccet-ml-datasets-${ENV}

    # Step 1: delete all object versions + delete markers
    # Paginate list-object-versions and batch-delete up to 1000 at a time
    aws --profile $PROFILE --region $REGION s3api list-object-versions \
        --bucket $BUCKET \
        --output json \
        --query '{Objects: Versions[].{Key:Key,VersionId:VersionId}}' \
        > /tmp/versions.json
    aws --profile $PROFILE --region $REGION s3api delete-objects \
        --bucket $BUCKET \
        --delete file:///tmp/versions.json

    aws --profile $PROFILE --region $REGION s3api list-object-versions \
        --bucket $BUCKET \
        --output json \
        --query '{Objects: DeleteMarkers[].{Key:Key,VersionId:VersionId}}' \
        > /tmp/markers.json
    aws --profile $PROFILE --region $REGION s3api delete-objects \
        --bucket $BUCKET \
        --delete file:///tmp/markers.json

    # Step 2: remove the bucket itself
    aws --profile $PROFILE --region $REGION s3 rb s3://$BUCKET
    ```
    Wrap the version-delete loop in a Python helper `scripts/delete_versioned_bucket.py` that takes `--environment` (required), resolves profile + region via `src.aws_config.AWSConfig.get_account(env)` (per Prompt 5 D4 — no hardcoded profile), accepts `--bucket` + `--dry-run`, and drives the pagination + batch-delete loop. Commit the helper as part of this task so stage/prod rollouts (Task 27) are repeatable with no script edits between environments.
  - [ ] 26.2 Empty and delete `ccet-ml-models-{env}` — same version-delete procedure (drift D2 confirms versioning=Enabled here too).
  - [ ] 26.3 Empty and delete `ccet-benchmark-reports-{env}` — versioning is NOT enabled here per `docs/s3-storage-structure.md`, so `aws s3 rm --recursive s3://ccet-benchmark-reports-{env}` + `aws s3 rb s3://ccet-benchmark-reports-{env}` is sufficient.
  - [ ] 26.4 Confirm the three old buckets no longer exist: `aws s3api list-buckets --query 'Buckets[?Name==`ccet-ml-datasets-dev` || Name==`ccet-ml-models-dev` || Name==`ccet-benchmark-reports-dev`]'` returns empty list.
  - *Design: "Sequence Diagrams" § "Phase 1 Deployment Sequence" step "aws s3 rb --force", "Risks and Mitigations" § Risk 7 (C4), "Post-Review Clarifications (Prompt 4)" § C4*
  - *Requirements: R9, R16*

## A. Execution Blockers Still Present

### A1. Design.md Testing Strategy § still contradicts Req 1.2 and Task 22

The revised Req 1.2 (and Task 22's `smoke_test_no_encryption`) accept AWS-default AES256 SSE-S3. But the design document's own **Testing Strategy § "Integration Testing Approach"** still contains the old wording:

> `smoke_test_no_encryption` — `s3api get-bucket-encryption` returns `ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError` (or the equivalent CDK `UNENCRYPTED` shape) and `s3api get-bucket-versioning` returns empty (not `Enabled`).

This directly contradicts Req 1.2 (which now says AES256 is "acceptable and expected") and Task 22 (which now says "Do NOT assert `ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError`").

**Three conflicting sources of truth exist for the same smoke test**:
- Req 1.2: AES256 OK, just no KmsKeyId
- Task 22: AES256 OK, no KmsKeyId, do NOT assert NotFoundError
- Design Testing Strategy §: assert NotFoundError

Kiro will almost certainly implement whichever it reads first.

**Fix**: update the Testing Strategy § paragraph in `design.md` to match Task 22's wording.

### A2. Task 24.2 still hardcodes `--profile bestehorn-learning`

Prompt 5 D4 explicitly required removing the hardcoded profile and resolving via `AWSConfig.get_account(env).profile`. Task 26.1 was updated. **Task 24.2 was not**:

```bash
aws --profile bestehorn-learning --region us-west-2 sagemaker list-training-jobs --status-equals InProgress
```

When Task 27.1 / 27.4 runs "Task 24 sequence with `--environment stage/prod`", this step will query the DEV account. Stage/prod rollout will silently measure the wrong account's job state.

**Fix**: rewrite 24.2 to resolve profile + region via `AWSConfig` (same pattern as 26.1), and make the wait step env-parameterized.

### A3. Task 23 references non-existent Req 15.3

Prompt 5 B3 removed the old Req 15.2 and renumbered Req 15.3 → Req 15.2. Task 14 reflects this correctly:
> "reviewer MUST confirm compatibility with the new bucket (Req 15.2 per Prompt 5 renumbering…)"

But Task 23 still says:
> "This is a WARN (not fail) with a review comment directing the reviewer to **Req 15.3** (confirm compatibility with the unencrypted new bucket)."

Req 15.3 no longer exists. Should be Req 15.2.

**Fix**: change `Req 15.3` → `Req 15.2` in Task 23.

### A4. Task 11 does not declare the `ssm_base_path` injection that Task 12 and Task 13 depend on

Tasks 12 and 13 both state:
> "Task 11 is updated to inject `ssm_base_path: '/ccet/{env}/storage/'` into the Lambda input."

But Task 11's own bullet list only covers:
- `BucketDeployment` `destination_key_prefix` change
- `s3_bucket` + `s3_key_prefix` hyperparameter change
- Training output path
- Two `PrefixScopedGrant` wirings

**It does not mention updating the Step Functions state machine definition to inject `ssm_base_path` into the Lambda invocation input payload.** This is a dependency gap — if Kiro processes Task 11 first without reading Tasks 12/13, it will not add the event-payload update.

**Fix**: add an explicit sub-bullet to Task 11: "Update the Step Functions state machine input transformer / task input to inject `ssm_base_path: '/ccet/{env}/storage/'` into the `data_export` and `registration` Lambda invocation events."

### A5. Task 9 does not declare the CloudWatch Events input-transformer update that Task 16 depends on

Symmetrical problem to A4. Task 16 says:
> "CDK update: configure the CloudWatch Events input transformer in `cdk/benchmarking_pipeline/constructs.py` to inject `ssm_base_path: '/ccet/{env}/storage/'` into the Lambda input"

But Task 9's bullet list does not include this update. The change should land in the CDK task (Task 9), not hang as an implicit prerequisite of Task 16.

**Fix**: add a sub-bullet to Task 9 specifying the input-transformer update.

## B. Material Gaps

### B1. Task 9a does not specify how the CI user stack imports the storage bucket

Task 9a prescribes `PrefixScopedGrant` on the CI user but doesn't say where the `s3.IBucket` comes from. The CI user stack (per `deployment_ordering.py`) has **no dependency on STORAGE** — it currently has `STACK_CI_USER: []`. Three plausible implementations exist:

1. Add `STACK_STORAGE` as a dep of `STACK_CI_USER` and pass `storage.bucket` via constructor injection.
2. Use `s3.Bucket.from_bucket_name(self, "StorageBucket", config.storage_bucket_name)` for a string-based import without a CFN dependency.
3. Skip `PrefixScopedGrant` entirely and hand-write `iam.PolicyStatement` with a literal ARN like `arn:aws:s3:::ccet-{env}/*`.

Each has different trade-offs (option 1 reorders the deploy graph; option 2 is simplest; option 3 bypasses the reusable construct). Kiro will pick one — probably not the one you want.

**Fix**: add one sentence to Task 9a specifying the chosen approach. Recommended: option 2 (string-based import via `from_bucket_name` — no CFN dep, keeps CI_USER at the top of DEPLOY_ORDER, works because IAM policies can reference ARNs of not-yet-created resources).

### B2. Req 3.1 enumeration count mismatch

Req 3.1 says "9 top-level prefixes" and then lists **10** items:

```
raw/, raw-errors/, processed/v1-horizon2min-window30min/, processed/v2-horizon30min-window60min/,
models/, code/, reports/, inference-logs/, archive/, temp/
```

The explanatory sentence reconciles this ("`processed/v1-…/` and `processed/v2-…/` share the single top-level `processed/` prefix but are enumerated explicitly"), but Correctness Property 10 in `design.md` lists **9** items with `processed/` counted once:

```
raw/, raw-errors/, processed/, models/, code/, reports/, inference-logs/, archive/, temp/
```

Both interpretations produce the same allowed-key set (because anything under `processed/v{N}-…/` is also under `processed/`), so this is not a semantic bug. But a smoke test that strictly enforces Req 3.1's 10-item enumeration vs. the design's 9-item list will produce different test code.

**Fix**: pick one form in Req 3.1. Either:
- Say "10 enumerated prefix paths covering 9 top-level categories", OR
- List 9 (with `processed/`) and note v1/v2 sub-prefixes in a footnote.

### B3. `scripts/delete_versioned_bucket.py` helper is referenced but not formally declared

Task 26.1 references this helper:
> "Wrap the version-delete loop in a Python helper `scripts/delete_versioned_bucket.py` that takes `--environment` (required)..."

But the helper is not listed in the **New Files** table of `design.md` (alongside `scripts/migrate_s3_storage.py` and `scripts/update_model_registry_bucket.py`). This means it has no explicit test target, is not covered by the Task 28.7 coverage assertion, and its existence as a deliverable is implicit.

**Fix**: add a row to design.md's "New Files" table; add a unit-test task under Task 26.

### B4. No task updates `src/ml/training/model_registry.py` Task 14 wording for `inference-logs/` comment

Task 14 says:
> "Update the code comment at lines 585-588 to reference the new `s3://ccet-{env}/inference-logs/{endpoint_name}/` destination URI pattern..."

This is specified correctly, but note this is the **only** place where the `inference-logs/` prefix is documented in code as the forward-compat destination. If Kiro skips Task 14's comment update and focuses only on the bucket-name SSM resolution, the forward-compat intent documented in Req 15 will be lost.

**Fix**: consider extracting the comment update into a separate sub-bullet under Task 14 (currently it's mixed into a paragraph about A4/A5 verification).

## C. Minor Clarifications

### C1. Correctness Property 5 still uses "No-encryption invariant" as its name

The correctness property name is "No-encryption invariant" but the body now accepts SSE-S3 AES256. The name is misleading — the invariant is actually "No customer-managed encryption invariant" or "No KMS invariant".

**Fix (optional)**: rename to "No-KMS-encryption invariant" to match the body.

### C2. Task 19.1 test does not explicitly cover the "sentinel NOT written when `all_verified=false`" path

Task 19.1 asserts the sentinel is written on success and the JSON report includes `force_ignore_training_jobs`. It does not assert:
- Sentinel is NOT written when `all_verified=false` (some mapping entry failed).
- Pre-existing sentinel is not accidentally overwritten on failure.

The design's ALGORITHM pseudocode correctly shows sentinel writing only in the `all_verified` branch, but no test enforces it.

**Fix**: add a sub-test case to 19.1: simulate a verification failure on one mapping entry, assert the script exits non-zero AND the SSM sentinel is NOT written.

### C3. Task 13a test case (c) and (b) are undistinguished in Task 19.1

Task 13a unit tests distinguish between:
- (b) "sentinel missing" → raise
- (c) "sentinel present but not valid JSON, or JSON without completed_at" → raise

But the error message for (b) vs (c) is semantically different (missing parameter vs. malformed value). Task 13a says tests should "distinguish the parse failure from the missing-parameter case" but the exception type or message distinction is not specified.

**Fix (minor)**: specify either two distinct exception subclasses or two distinct error-message prefixes for (b) vs (c).

### C4. Task 24.7 implicitly assumes `--skip-migration-check` is NOT passed

Task 24.7 runs `python cdk/deploy.py dev` after migration completes. The pre-flight (Task 13a) now reads the sentinel and passes. This is correct, but:

If a previous run wrote a sentinel with `completed_at` but the JSON is corrupted (e.g., truncated write), Task 24.7's deploy will fail with a parse error, which is correct. But the recovery path (re-run migration? delete the sentinel and re-run? use `--skip-migration-check`?) is not documented.

**Fix (minor)**: add a note under Task 24.7 or under Task 13a describing the recovery playbook when the sentinel is corrupted.

## 1. Introduction

This specification consolidates all project-owned S3 storage for the CCET trading bot into a single bucket per environment (`ccet-{env}`), with a fixed prefix taxonomy, uniform bucket policies, and least-privilege prefix-scoped IAM. Phase 1 covers storage consolidation only; a future Phase 2 will add a re-drive mechanism.

## 2. Scope

### 2.1 In Scope

- New `CCETStorage-{Env}` CloudFormation stack owning `ccet-{env}`.
- One lifecycle rule on the new bucket: `temp/` prefix, 14-day expiration.
- Uniform bucket-level policies: SSL-only, `BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL`, no encryption, no versioning, project tags.
- Data migration from three existing CDK-managed buckets to the new bucket (one-shot, idempotent).
- Retargeting of every writer and reader (CDK + Lambda + scripts) to the new bucket and new prefixes.
- Fix of drift D3 (DQN training data misplaced under `ccet-ml-models-{env}/training-data/`).
- Fix of drift D5 (dead `MLDataConfig.s3_bucket` field cleanup).
- Deletion of 2021 legacy buckets (`ccet`, `ccet-test`).
- Deletion of three old project buckets post-migration verification.

### 2.2 Out of Scope (Non-Goals)

- No changes to the processing pipeline trigger mechanism (DynamoDB Streams → V1/V2 Processing Lambdas stays identical).
- No re-drive mechanism (Phase 2).
- No encryption, no versioning, no KMS on the new bucket.
- No changes to shared AWS-managed buckets (`cdk-hnb659fds-assets-*`, `sagemaker-{region}-{account}`).
- No DynamoDB schema changes.
- No Bitfinex API client changes.
- No changes to `MLDataConfig` other than the D5 field removal.

---

## 3. Functional Requirements

### Requirement 1 — New Storage Stack Creates the Consolidated Bucket

**User Story**: As an operator, I want a single `ccet-{env}` bucket per environment, so that all project data lives in one place with one policy to reason about.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** `cdk deploy CCETStorage-{Env}` succeeds, **THEN** exactly one `AWS::S3::Bucket` is created with `BucketName="ccet-{env}"`.
2. **WHEN** `aws s3api get-bucket-encryption` is invoked on the new bucket, **THEN** the response MUST NOT contain any `KmsKeyId` or `KmsMasterKeyID`. The AWS-default server-side encryption with Amazon S3-managed keys (SSE-S3 / AES256) is acceptable and expected per AWS's post-2023 default-encryption policy (see [AWS S3 Protecting data with encryption docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingEncryption.html): *"Amazon S3 now applies server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) as the base level of encryption for every bucket in Amazon S3. Starting January 5, 2023, all new object uploads to Amazon S3 are automatically encrypted..."*). "No encryption" in this spec's original phrasing is interpreted as "no customer-managed KMS key and no configured KMS-based default encryption" — the automatic AES256 applied by S3 to new buckets cannot be disabled. (Revised per Prompt 5 A7.)
3. **WHEN** `aws s3api get-bucket-versioning` is invoked on the new bucket, **THEN** the `Status` field is empty (not `Enabled`, not `Suspended`).
4. **WHEN** `aws s3api get-public-access-block` is invoked, **THEN** all four flags (`BlockPublicAcls`, `IgnorePublicAcls`, `BlockPublicPolicy`, `RestrictPublicBuckets`) return `true`.
5. **WHEN** `aws s3api get-bucket-policy` is invoked, **THEN** the policy contains a `Deny` statement on `aws:SecureTransport=false` covering both the bucket and its contents.
6. **WHEN** `aws s3api get-bucket-tagging` is invoked, **THEN** the tag set contains exactly `Project=CCET`, `Environment={env}`, `ManagedBy=CDK`, `Owner=ccet-team`. `CostCenter` is explicitly absent per Prompt 2 answer (1).
7. **WHEN** the environment is `dev` and the stack is destroyed, **THEN** the bucket and its contents are deleted (`auto_delete_objects=True`, `removal_policy=DESTROY`).
8. **WHEN** the environment is `stage` or `prod`, **THEN** the bucket has `removal_policy=RETAIN` and `auto_delete_objects=False`.

### Requirement 2 — Exactly One Lifecycle Rule Is Applied

**User Story**: As an operator, I want a single, simple lifecycle policy so that retention rules are trivially auditable.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** `aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration` is invoked on `ccet-{env}`, **THEN** exactly one `Rule` is returned.
2. **WHEN** that rule is inspected, **THEN** `Filter.Prefix == "temp/"` and `Expiration.Days == 14` and `Status == "Enabled"`.
3. **WHEN** an object is PUT to `temp/` with a creation date more than 14 days in the past (simulated via lifecycle test), **THEN** S3 expires it on the next lifecycle evaluation.
4. **WHEN** an object is PUT to any non-`temp/` prefix, **THEN** no transition or expiration action is scheduled.

### Requirement 3 — Prefix Taxonomy Is Fixed and Exclusive

**User Story**: As a developer, I want every object written by the project to live under a known, documented prefix so that future data-operations work is mechanical.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** any CCET writer performs a `PutObject` post-cutover, **THEN** the object key MUST start with one of the **10 enumerated prefix paths covering 9 top-level categories** (revised per Prompt 6 B2): `raw/`, `raw-errors/`, `processed/v1-horizon2min-window30min/`, `processed/v2-horizon30min-window60min/`, `models/`, `code/`, `reports/`, `inference-logs/`, `archive/`, `temp/`. The two `processed/v{N}-…/` paths share the single top-level `processed/` category but are enumerated as distinct paths because each is the destination of a distinct Firehose delivery stream (V1 and V2). Correctness Property 10 in `design.md` counts the 9 top-level categories (`processed/` counted once); both views are consistent — any `processed/v1-…/*` or `processed/v2-…/*` key satisfies both the 10-path enumeration above AND Correctness Property 10's 9-category form (since any such key starts with `processed/`). Smoke tests implementing Req 3.2 SHOULD enforce the 10-path form to catch taxonomy drift (e.g., a writer using `processed/v3-…/` would pass the 9-category form but fail the 10-path form).
2. **WHEN** any writer attempts to write outside these prefixes, **THEN** the IAM policy denies the request (verified by smoke test).
3. **IF** a future prefix is required, **THEN** it MUST be added to the design document first (no silent taxonomy expansion).

### Requirement 4 — IAM Is Least-Privilege and Prefix-Scoped

**User Story**: As a security owner, I want every principal's S3 access limited to the narrowest possible prefix so that blast radius of any credential compromise is minimized.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** CDK synth produces IAM policies for any CCET principal, **THEN** no statement has `Action="s3:*"`.
2. **WHEN** CDK synth produces IAM policies for any CCET principal, **THEN** no statement has `Resource` matching `arn:aws:s3:::ccet-{env}/*` without a prefix qualifier.
3. **WHEN** a principal needs multiple prefixes, **THEN** its IAM policy enumerates each prefix in a separate statement (or in a `Resource` list).
4. **FOR EACH** row in the IAM Prefix Matrix in `design.md`, the synthesized IAM policy matches the documented access level (read / write / delete / list).
5. **WHEN** a `s3:ListBucket` permission is granted, **THEN** it is scoped via a `Condition { StringLike: { "s3:prefix": [...] } }` listing the allowed prefixes.

### Requirement 5 — All Writers Are Retargeted to the New Bucket

**User Story**: As an operator, after Phase 1 is deployed, I should see no new objects arriving in the three old buckets, and all expected prefixes populated on the new bucket.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** the DataCollector Lambda runs post-cutover, **THEN** the raw-archive Firehose writes to `s3://ccet-{env}/raw/*` (not `s3://ccet-ml-datasets-{env}/raw/*`).
2. **WHEN** the V1 Data Processing Lambda runs post-cutover, **THEN** the V1 Firehose writes to `s3://ccet-{env}/processed/v1-horizon2min-window30min/*`.
3. **WHEN** the V2 Data Processing Lambda runs post-cutover, **THEN** the V2 Firehose writes to `s3://ccet-{env}/processed/v2-horizon30min-window60min/*`.
4. **WHEN** the Benchmark Metrics Lambda runs post-cutover, **THEN** it writes reports to `s3://ccet-{env}/reports/daily/*`.
5. **WHEN** the RL Data Export Lambda runs post-cutover, **THEN** it writes to `s3://ccet-{env}/temp/rl-training-exports/*` (fixes drift D3).
6. **WHEN** a SageMaker DQN training job runs post-cutover, **THEN** model outputs are written to `s3://ccet-{env}/models/dqn/{version}/*`.
7. **IF** any SageMaker endpoint writes data capture records post-cutover, **THEN** records MUST land under `s3://ccet-{env}/inference-logs/*`. (Revised per Prompt 5 B4 — current deployment uses SageMaker Serverless Inference which does not support DataCaptureConfig per Req 15.1, so this clause is vacuous today; it becomes active if/when a real-time instance-based endpoint is introduced.)

### Requirement 6 — All Readers Are Retargeted to the New Bucket

**User Story**: As an operator, post-cutover, every read path should resolve from the new bucket with no fallback to old buckets.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** the DQN Model Manager loads a model, **THEN** it reads from `s3://ccet-{env}/models/dqn/*`.
2. **WHEN** the XGBoost Model Manager loads a model, **THEN** it reads from `s3://ccet-{env}/models/XGBoost/*`.
3. **WHEN** the RL Registration Lambda verifies artifacts, **THEN** it reads from `s3://ccet-{env}/models/*`.
4. **WHEN** `src/ml/training/data_loader.py` loads training data, **THEN** it reads from `s3://ccet-{env}/processed/v2-horizon30min-window60min/*` (default) or the prefix configured via SSM `/ccet/{env}/ml/training/training_data_prefix`.
5. **WHEN** a SageMaker training job starts, **THEN** it reads its source tarball from `s3://ccet-{env}/code/latest/sourcedir.tar.gz`.
6. **WHEN** `grep -rn "ccet-ml-datasets\|ccet-ml-models\|ccet-benchmark-reports" src/ cdk/ scripts/` is run after the refactor, **THEN** no matches are found outside this spec's documentation files.

### Requirement 7 — Data Is Migrated Without Loss

**User Story**: As an operator, I want every object from the three old buckets present on the new bucket before writer cutover so that no data is lost.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** `python scripts/migrate_s3_storage.py --environment {env}` completes successfully, **THEN** the script's JSON report shows `all_verified=true` and every mapping entry's `source_object_count == destination_object_count`.
2. **FOR EACH** mapping row in `design.md` § "Low-Level Design — Migration Script" § "Authoritative mapping":
   - every object under the source prefix has a corresponding object at the destination prefix with identical **object count** AND identical **per-object byte size** (measured by `ListObjectsV2.Size`). (Revised from the original "byte-for-byte" wording per Prompt 4 item C2. ETag comparison is not reliable across multipart uploads and was never implemented. The `aws s3 sync --exact-timestamps` command used internally compares size + last-modified, which is consistent with this acceptance criterion.)
3. **WHEN** the migration script is run with `--dry-run`, **THEN** no S3 API call that modifies state is made (verified by mocking `subprocess.run` in unit tests).
4. **WHEN** the migration script is run twice back-to-back (idempotency), **THEN** the second run's report shows zero additional copies and `all_verified=true`.
5. **WHEN** any source bucket is inaccessible or a sync fails, **THEN** the script exits non-zero and the JSON report records the failing entry.
6. **WHEN** the migration script completes successfully on all mapping entries, **THEN** it writes a sentinel SSM parameter `/ccet/{env}/storage/migration-complete` with the **canonical JSON value defined in Req 18.4** (shape: `{"completed_at": "<ISO-8601>", "script_version": "<git-sha-or-tag>", "mapping_entries_verified": <int>}`). The plain-string `"true"` form is NOT accepted. (Revised per Prompt 5 A1 — single canonical format.)
7. **WHEN** the migration script copies data from a versioning-enabled source bucket (`ccet-ml-datasets-{env}` and `ccet-ml-models-{env}` have `Versioning=Enabled` per drifts D1/D2), **THEN** only current object versions are migrated. Noncurrent versions and delete markers are NOT migrated and are discarded when the source buckets are deleted in Task 26. (Per Prompt 5 A6 userInput decision — option a: the new bucket is `versioned=False`, and historical noncurrent versions are treated as ephemeral snapshots. This loss is explicitly accepted by the user.)

### Requirement 8 — Legacy 2021 Buckets Are Deleted

**User Story**: As a security owner, I want the 2021 legacy buckets (`ccet`, `ccet-test`) removed from the account to reduce attack surface.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** Phase 1 completes on the dev account, **THEN** `aws s3api list-buckets` does not return `ccet` or `ccet-test`.
2. **WHEN** any script in this repository references `s3://ccet/` or `s3://ccet-test/`, **THEN** the reference is treated as a bug and MUST be removed.
3. Authorization for deletion is granted by the user per Prompt 2 answer (4).

### Requirement 9 — Old Project Buckets Are Deleted Post-Migration

**User Story**: As an operator, after migration verification and smoke-test success, I want the three old project buckets removed so that only the consolidated bucket remains.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** smoke tests pass against the new bucket and no CANDIDATE model-registry records reference an old bucket, **THEN** `ccet-ml-datasets-{env}`, `ccet-ml-models-{env}`, and `ccet-benchmark-reports-{env}` are deleted.
2. Deletion requires a prior CDK code change to replace `RemovalPolicy.RETAIN` with `RemovalPolicy.DESTROY` (and for the benchmark-reports bucket, the bucket definition is removed entirely since its data is migrated).
3. **FOR EACH** old bucket: `aws s3api list-buckets` MUST NOT return it after Phase 1 completes.

### Requirement 10 — Driftly D3 Is Fixed (DQN Training Data Relocation)

**User Story**: As a future operator, I want all training data under a consistent prefix so that I can enumerate it without knowing service-specific history.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** the RL Data Export Lambda runs post-cutover, **THEN** it writes to `s3://ccet-{env}/temp/rl-training-exports/{pair}/{job_id}/` (NOT `s3://ccet-ml-models-{env}/training-data/{pair}/{job_id}/`).
2. **WHEN** `src/lambdas/rl_training_pipeline/data_export_handler.py` is inspected, **THEN** the `s3_bucket` return value reads from SSM `/ccet/{env}/storage/bucket-name` (no hardcoded `ccet-ml-models-{env}`).
3. **WHEN** CDK synth is run on `CCETRlTrainingPipelineStack`, **THEN** the RL Data Export Lambda's IAM policy grants write access to `temp/rl-training-exports/*` only (not `training-data/*` on `ccet-ml-models-{env}`).

### Requirement 11 — Drift D5 Is Fixed (Dead Config Field Cleanup)

**User Story**: As a developer, I want dead config fields removed so that they don't mislead future readers.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** `src/core/ml_config.py` is inspected, **THEN** the `s3_bucket = "ccet-training-data"` field is absent.
2. **WHEN** `grep -rn 'MLDataConfig.s3_bucket' src/ cdk/ scripts/ test/` is run, **THEN** no matches are found.
3. **WHEN** `pytest test/` runs, **THEN** no test depends on the removed field.

### Requirement 12 — Rollout Is Environment-Parameterized

**User Story**: As an operator, I want the same Phase 1 changes to deploy to dev, stage, and prod via the same command (different `{env}` arg) so that rollout is repeatable.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** `python cdk/deploy.py {env}` is invoked for any supported `{env}` in `config/aws_accounts.json`, **THEN** the deployment succeeds with no env-specific code branches.
2. **WHEN** the migration script is invoked with any supported `{env}`, **THEN** it resolves the AWS profile + region from `src.aws_config.AWSConfig.get_account({env})`.
3. **WHEN** `cdk/deployment/deployment_ordering.py` is inspected, **THEN** `STACK_STORAGE` is registered with no dependencies, and every other stack that uses S3 declares `STACK_STORAGE` as a dependency.

### Requirement 13 — Deploy Orchestrator Enforces Migration Ordering

**User Story**: As an operator, I want the deploy script to stop me from deploying downstream stacks before the storage stack + migration is complete, so that I can't accidentally corrupt data.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** `cdk/deploy.py` is invoked and `CCETStorage-{Env}` does not exist yet, **THEN** all downstream deploys are blocked until `CCETStorage-{Env}` is deployed first (handled by the dependency graph in `deployment_ordering.py`).
2. **WHEN** `cdk/deploy.py` is invoked and the SSM parameter `/ccet/{env}/storage/bucket-name` exists but the sentinel parameter `/ccet/{env}/storage/migration-complete` is absent OR does not parse as the canonical JSON defined in Req 18.4 (specifically: the parsed JSON value MUST have a `completed_at` field), **THEN** the orchestrator fails with a clear error instructing the operator to run `scripts/migrate_s3_storage.py --environment {env}` before proceeding. (Revised from "prints an explicit warning" per Prompt 4 item A3 — this is now a hard gate. Revised from the previous "is NOT `\"true\"`" phrasing per Prompt 5 A1 — the canonical shape is JSON per Req 18.4; no plain-string `"true"` fallback is accepted.)
3. **WHEN** the operator invokes `cdk/deploy.py --skip-migration-check {env}`, **THEN** the pre-flight check is bypassed (for re-deploys after migration). The `--skip-migration-check` flag is now a committed implementation requirement, not optional. (Per Prompt 4 item C5.)
4. **WHEN** `scripts/migrate_s3_storage.py --environment {env}` completes successfully, **THEN** it writes the sentinel parameter `/ccet/{env}/storage/migration-complete` using the canonical JSON value defined in Req 18.4 via `ssm.put_parameter(Overwrite=True)`. (Revised per Prompt 5 A1 — references Req 18.4 as the single source of truth for the sentinel shape; no plain-string `"true"` form is accepted.)

### Requirement 14 — Model Registry Records Point to the New Bucket

**User Story**: As an RL pipeline operator, I want all CANDIDATE records in the model registry to reference `ccet-{env}` post-migration so that promotion/rollback continues to work.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** a one-shot update script `scripts/update_model_registry_bucket.py --environment {env}` completes, **THEN** every record in `ccet-model-registry-{env}` with `s3_bucket=ccet-ml-models-{env}` is updated to:
   - `s3_bucket=ccet-{env}`, AND
   - `s3_prefix` remapped per the migration mapping (e.g. a record with `s3_prefix=training-data/{pair}/{job_id}/` is updated to `s3_prefix=temp/rl-training-exports/{pair}/{job_id}/`; a record with `s3_prefix=models/dqn/{version}/` keeps its prefix). (Revised per Prompt 4 item C3 — the original phrasing "preserving `s3_prefix`" was incorrect because `training-data/*` maps to `temp/rl-training-exports/*`, not to itself.)
2. **WHEN** a new CANDIDATE record is created by `registration_handler.py` post-cutover, **THEN** `s3_bucket=ccet-{env}` and `s3_prefix=models/dqn/{version}/`.
3. **WHEN** the old `ccet-ml-models-{env}` bucket is deleted, **THEN** no live registry record references it.

### Requirement 15 — SageMaker Endpoint DataCaptureConfig Forward Compatibility (NEW — Prompt 4 A4/A5)

**User Story**: As a future operator, when real-time instance-based SageMaker endpoints are introduced, I want data-capture logs to land under `inference-logs/` on the new bucket (not under any legacy path).

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **Investigation result — baseline state**: In the current codebase, `src/ml/training/model_registry.py` lines 585-588 explicitly state SageMaker Serverless Inference does not support DataCaptureConfig, and no existing endpoint writes to the old `ccet-ml-models-{env}/data-capture/` prefix. The migration mapping entry for `data-capture/` → `inference-logs/` will therefore copy zero objects in current deployments. **No SageMaker endpoint re-deployment or UpdateEndpoint call is required** as part of Phase 1 — contrary to the Prompt 4 A4 concern.
2. **WHEN** any code change introduces a `KmsKeyId` parameter in endpoint or DataCaptureConfig creation, **THEN** a reviewer MUST confirm the new bucket does not require KMS (new bucket has no customer KMS key per Req 1.2 — AWS-default SSE-S3 only), either by updating the bucket encryption config in the same PR or by removing the KMS parameter. A CI guardrail in Task 23 flags new occurrences of `KmsKeyId` in SageMaker-related source files.

> **Note (Prompt 5 B3)**: the previous Req 15.2 ("WHEN future code re-enables DataCaptureConfig for real-time endpoints, THEN the `DestinationS3Uri` MUST resolve to `s3://ccet-{env}/inference-logs/{endpoint_name}/`") has been **moved to `design.md` § "Post-Review Clarifications (Prompt 5)" § B3** as a forward-compatibility design note. That clause described future code behavior that cannot be tested today and therefore should not be a Phase 1 acceptance criterion. The acceptance criteria above are the only Phase 1–verifiable obligations for Req 15; the forward-compat note in design.md is informative, not a requirement.

### Requirement 16 — End-to-End Runtime Verification Gates Bucket Deletion (NEW — Prompt 4 Task 29)

**User Story**: As an operator, I want every pipeline (DataCollector → Firehose → raw/, DDB Streams → V1/V2 processing → processed/, decision Lambdas → DynamoDB, DQN/XGBoost model loading, benchmark metrics → reports/) verified to write and read from the new bucket **before** any legacy bucket is deleted, so that I catch any missed retargeting while rollback via re-sync is still possible.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** Task 29 (end-to-end verification) runs successfully per the sub-tasks 29.1 through 29.13 in `tasks.md`, **THEN** Tasks 25 (legacy bucket deletion) and 26 (old project bucket deletion) are permitted to proceed. The evidence bundle at `tmp/evidence/e2e/{env}-{timestamp}/` captures all pass/fail verifications.
2. **WHEN** any sub-task of Task 29 fails, **THEN** Task 25 and Task 26 MUST NOT be executed until the failure is resolved and Task 29 is re-run end-to-end with PASS.
3. **FOR EACH** writer category (DataCollector, V1 Processing, V2 Processing, RL Data Export, Benchmark Metrics, SageMaker training), Task 29 verifies at least one object was written to the expected prefix on `ccet-{env}` AND zero new objects arrived at the corresponding prefix on the old bucket during the verification window.
4. **FOR EACH** reader category (DQN Model Manager, XGBoost Model Manager, RL Registration, XGBoost data_loader, SageMaker training-job source download), Task 29 verifies a successful read from the new bucket path.
5. **NEGATIVE VERIFICATION**: Task 29 attempts an explicit `PutObject` to the old `ccet-ml-datasets-{env}` / `ccet-ml-models-{env}` / `ccet-benchmark-reports-{env}` buckets from a principal that previously had write access, and asserts the request is denied (either by IAM revocation or by bucket emptiness prerequisite). Similarly, attempts an HTTP (not HTTPS) PUT to the new bucket and asserts `AccessDenied`.

### Requirement 17 — Legacy Backup Data Is Preserved Indefinitely (NEW — Prompt 4 A8)

**User Story**: As an operator who explicitly designated `training-data-backup/` as my safety net during this migration, I want that data preserved indefinitely (not subject to the 14-day `temp/` expiration).

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** the migration script runs, **THEN** data from `ccet-ml-datasets-{env}/training-data-backup/` is copied to `ccet-{env}/archive/legacy-training-data-backup/` (NOT under `temp/`).
2. **WHEN** `s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration` is invoked on `ccet-{env}`, **THEN** no lifecycle rule matches the `archive/` prefix. Only the single `temp/` → 14d-expiration rule exists.
3. **WHEN** `docs/storage.md` is inspected, **THEN** it documents that the `archive/` prefix is retained indefinitely and that `training-data-backup/` was moved there specifically to preserve user-designated recovery data.

### Requirement 18 — Migration Pre-Flight Checks (NEW — Prompt 4 A3, B3)

**User Story**: As an operator, I want the migration and deployment sequence to refuse to proceed if the account is in an unsafe state (in-flight SageMaker jobs, missing migration sentinel), so I don't cause data loss.

**Acceptance Criteria**:

1. **WHEN** `scripts/migrate_s3_storage.py --environment {env}` is invoked and there is at least one SageMaker training job with `TrainingJobStatus=InProgress` or HPO tuning job with `HyperParameterTuningJobStatus=InProgress`, **THEN** the script exits non-zero with an error listing the in-flight jobs. A `--force-ignore-training-jobs` flag bypasses this (for stage/prod where an operator has made the explicit risk call). (Per Prompt 4 B3.)
2. **WHEN** `cdk/deploy.py {env}` is invoked without `--skip-migration-check` and `CCETStorage-{Env}` exists but `/ccet/{env}/storage/migration-complete` is absent, or the parameter value does not parse as JSON, or the parsed JSON is missing a non-empty `completed_at` field, **THEN** the deploy exits non-zero with an error instructing the operator to run migration. (Per Prompt 4 A3, C5, revised per Prompt 5 A1 — canonical JSON per Req 18.4; no plain-string `"true"` fallback.)
3. **WHEN** `cdk/deploy.py {env} --skip-migration-check` is invoked, **THEN** the pre-flight check is skipped (for post-migration re-deploys).
4. **WHEN** `scripts/migrate_s3_storage.py` writes the `/ccet/{env}/storage/migration-complete` sentinel, **THEN** the value is JSON with shape `{"completed_at": "<ISO-8601>", "script_version": "<git-sha-or-tag>", "mapping_entries_verified": <int>}` so the pre-flight check can audit the completion record, not just the boolean.

---

## 4. Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-1 — Cost Neutrality

The consolidation must not materially increase S3 storage cost. Migrating data via `aws s3 sync` transfers bytes but does not duplicate long-term storage (old buckets are deleted after verification). One-time migration transfer cost is expected to be negligible for dev.

### NFR-2 — Availability

No downtime on the data collection or decision pipelines. The cutover uses CloudFormation's in-place Firehose destination update (sub-minute) — DynamoDB remains authoritative throughout.

### NFR-3 — Observability

- The migration script writes an auditable JSON report to `tmp/evidence/s3-migration/{env}-{timestamp}.json`.
- CDK synth output is reviewable via `cdk diff` prior to deploy.
- Smoke tests verify the end-state configuration post-deploy.

### NFR-4 — Documentation

- `docs/storage.md` documents the new taxonomy, IAM matrix, and lifecycle.
- `docs/s3-storage-structure.md` is updated or superseded to reflect the post-Phase-1 state.
- `docs/forLLMConsumption.md` is updated with the new bucket naming convention.

### NFR-5 — Reversibility

Until the old buckets are deleted (Requirement 9), rollback is possible by reverting the CDK changes and reverting the Firehose destinations. Post-deletion, rollback requires restoring from backup (out of scope for Phase 1 — explicitly accepted risk).

### NFR-6 — Test Coverage

All new code ships with unit tests and, where applicable, property-based tests per workspace rules. Minimum 80% coverage as per `post-activity.md`.

---

## 5. Acceptance Criteria Summary

Phase 1 is considered complete when all the following are simultaneously true on the target environment:

- [ ] `ccet-{env}` bucket exists with the properties specified in Requirement 1.
- [ ] Exactly one lifecycle rule (Requirement 2).
- [ ] Every writer writes to the new bucket with the correct prefix (Requirement 5).
- [ ] Every reader reads from the new bucket (Requirement 6).
- [ ] Migration script report shows `all_verified=true` with size-parity verification (Requirement 7).
- [ ] Migration-complete sentinel written (Req 7.6, Req 13.4).
- [ ] `ccet` and `ccet-test` are deleted (Requirement 8).
- [ ] `ccet-ml-datasets-{env}`, `ccet-ml-models-{env}`, `ccet-benchmark-reports-{env}` are deleted (Requirement 9).
- [ ] Drift D3 (Requirement 10) and drift D5 (Requirement 11) are fixed.
- [ ] Same deploy command works for dev/stage/prod (Requirement 12).
- [ ] Deploy pre-flight blocks on missing migration (Requirement 13).
- [ ] Model registry records remapped per migration mapping (Requirement 14).
- [ ] Future-compat audit of SageMaker DataCaptureConfig documented (Requirement 15).
- [ ] End-to-end runtime verification (Task 29) PASS before any legacy-bucket deletion (Requirement 16).
- [ ] `archive/legacy-training-data-backup/` populated with no lifecycle rule (Requirement 17).
- [ ] Migration and deploy pre-flight checks block on unsafe states (Requirement 18).
- [ ] All new code has tests passing; `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy`, `pylint`, `bandit` all pass.
- [ ] `docs/storage.md` exists and documents the new taxonomy (including `archive/` and the 14-day retention policy for `temp/`).

<design>
# Design Document: S3 Storage Consolidation — Phase 1

> **Scope**: Phase 1 of a two-phase effort to consolidate all project-owned S3 storage into a single bucket per environment (`ccet-{env}`) with a clean prefix taxonomy, uniform bucket policies, and least-privilege prefix-scoped IAM. Phase 2 (re-drive mechanism) is explicitly out of scope.
>
> **Design detail level**: Both High-Level Design (architecture diagrams, bucket/prefix taxonomy, IAM matrix, migration data flow) AND Low-Level Design (CDK construct signatures, migration script pseudocode, IAM policy document shapes, file-by-file change details). The user's original request explicitly selected both artifacts.
>
> **Authoritative source for decisions**: The user's verbatim specification (documented in the "User Prompts" section at the end of this document) defines the scope, taxonomy, lifecycle policy, migration mapping, and IAM matrix. This design elaborates the *how* — not the *what*.
